titleTr: Okulun tarihi: was built, were donated

grammar.topic: Simple passive (past): was / were + past participle
explainTr: Geçmişte yapılmış bir işi, yapanı söylemeden anlatmak için geçmiş edilgen kullanırız: The school was built in 1952. Yapı: was/were + fiilin 3. hali (V3).
Tekil özne için was, çoğul özne için were: The gym was added. The windows were replaced. Olumsuz: wasn't/weren't. Soru: When was the school established?
Yapanı söylemek istersen 'by' eklenir: The library was opened by the mayor. Okulun, şehrin, binanın tarihini anlatırken bu yapıyı çok kullanırsın.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'yapıldı', 'açıldı', 'bağışlandı' gibi -ıldı ekleri vardır. İngilizcede ek yerine was/were + V3 kullanırsın: was built, were donated. 'The school built in 1952' (be fiilini unutmak) Türkçeden gelen çok yaygın bir hatadır.

reading.title: The history of Lincoln Elementary
reading.text:
In the front hall of Lincoln Elementary, there is a big photo of an old brick building. Today Hafsa stops to read the plaque next to it.

The school was established in 1952. It was named after Abraham Lincoln, and it was built by the local community. Many families donated money, and neighbors helped with the work. The first classes were held in just four rooms. Only eighty students were enrolled in the first year, and most of them walked to school.

In 1975, the building was expanded, and a gym was added. The old wooden windows were replaced in 1998, and the library was renovated in 2015. New computers were bought, and soft chairs were placed in the reading corner. Every year, the school's anniversary is celebrated with a big picnic on the playground.

At the bottom of the plaque, Hafsa reads a list of names. These people were honored because they worked at the school for more than thirty years. One name is "Mrs. Dolores Green, secretary, 1968-2001."

Hafsa takes a photo with her phone. "This is not only a school," she thinks. "It is the history of a community. Maybe one day my name will be on a list like this one."

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: Linda, did you know Lincoln Elementary was built in 1952?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Of course! I went there in the late 1970s. The gym was brand new then, but there was no real library.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: No library? Where were the books kept?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: In boxes in the hallway! The library was opened in 1990, after I left.

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Lunch was brought from home in paper bags. The cafeteria was built much later.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: And how were the children taken to school?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Most of us walked. Only a few were taken by bus.

script.speaker: Hafsa
script.text: I love these stories. Can I write them down?

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Of course. Maybe they will be put on the school website one day!

script.speaker: Linda
script.text: Then I will bring you my old school photos next week.

writing.promptTr: Bildiğin bir yerin (okulun, mahallenin, bir binanın) geçmişini edilgen geçmiş zamanla anlat. En az beş was/were + V3 cümlesi kur.
writing.promptEn: Write about the history of a place you know, such as your school or a building. Use at least five past passive sentences.
writing.model: My school in Isparta was built in 1962. It was a small, white building with ten classrooms. The garden was planted by the students and teachers. Every spring, flowers were put around the door. In 1990, a new gym was added, and the old windows were replaced. Many years later, a library was opened, and hundreds of books were donated by local families. I was taught to read in that school. On its 50th anniversary, a big party was held, and our old teachers were invited. I was so happy to see them again.
